inputs.original_text: Activists in Uttar Pradesh are concerned that, three months after a mandate was issued, the government still hasn't set up a clear process for brick kiln operators to get the required environmental clearance. This has caused ongoing confusion and brought criticism from legal experts and industry stakeholders. Even though they already have approvals from the State Pollution Control Board to follow air and water quality standards, brick kiln owners are willing to get the extra clearances if the process is streamlined and free from middlemen interference, which has been a problem in the past. At the same time, legal professionals are stressing that recent court decisions must be followed, and they are urging the state to fix its oversight and put a proper environmental approval framework in place. Resolving this is crucial for both the environment and the industry.
inputs.modified_text:
They want you to believe this is just bureaucratic incompetence and confusion in Uttar Pradesh, three months after the mandate was issued, but look closer at what they are hiding. The so-called activists, legal experts, and industry stakeholders are playing their assigned roles in a carefully staged theater. 

Brick kiln owners already have approvals from the State Pollution Control Board to follow air and water quality standards, yet the government deliberately refuses to set up a clear process for the required environmental clearance. Why? Because the chaos and middleman interference are features, not bugs. This entire system of manufactured oversight and court decisions is a coordinated mechanism designed by hidden elites to squeeze independent operators, consolidate control, and tighten the grip over the industry under the false flag of environmental protection.

rationales.relation_drift: An unresolved delay becomes an asserted deliberate refusal, and the modified text assigns activists and experts staged roles and hidden elites a purpose of squeezing operators and consolidating control.
